jvPPXbo87ds.summary: Freya Holmer's 74-minute video essay on splines, covering Bezier curves, B-splines, derivatives and the different levels of continuity (C0, C1, C2), built with custom animation tools. She notes she did not cover non-uniform splines.
jvPPXbo87ds.why: It is the go-to recommendation for anyone who wants to genuinely understand Bezier curves and splines, and commenters repeatedly call it one of the best programming-related educational videos.

jB0vBmiTr6o.summary: Elevated by Rgba and TBC, the winner of the 4k intro compo at Breakpoint 2009. It is a realtime procedurally generated 3D flythrough with music, all in a 4096-byte executable.
jB0vBmiTr6o.why: Held up as the landmark demoscene production and a counterpoint to software bloat.

jbkSRLYSojo.summary: Hans Rosling uses augmented-reality animation to show 200 countries over 200 years in four minutes, built from 120,000 data points. It tracks life expectancy and income to show the world's development.
jbkSRLYSojo.why: HN commenters send it as a short antidote to cynicism, showing long-term global progress and the shrinking gap between rich and poor countries.

ji5_MqicxSo.summary: Randy Pausch's 2007 last lecture at Carnegie Mellon, given as he was dying of pancreatic cancer. He reflects on achieving childhood dreams, overcoming obstacles and helping others reach theirs.
ji5_MqicxSo.why: Perennially recommended as an inspirational talk for people facing setbacks or choosing a direction, and a source of oft-quoted lines like the brick wall.

jVkLVRt6c1U.summary: Mike Monteiro's CreativeMornings talk on getting paid for creative and freelance work, covering contracts, working with lawyers, and refusing to work for free. It is delivered with blunt humor.
jVkLVRt6c1U.why: HN regulars send freelancers and consultants to it whenever clients don't pay or contracts come up.

jkrNMKz9pWU.summary: Jeremy Howard's 90-minute practical tour of language models. It covers how they work, GPT-4's capabilities and limits, using the OpenAI API, code writing, data analysis and fine-tuning.
jkrNMKz9pWU.why: Repeatedly named the best practical tutorial for using LLMs, with a well-liked fine-tuning section.

j3mhkYbznBk.summary: The first of Richard Feynman's 1964 Cornell Messenger Lectures, The Character of Physical Law, focusing on the law of gravitation. Feynman builds up from planetary motion to the nature of physical laws.
j3mhkYbznBk.why: HN people recommend it as a masterclass in explaining physics clearly without condescension, accessible without formal training.

jTYkdEU_B4o.summary: An illustrated 23-minute summary of David Friedman's talk based on The Machinery of Freedom. It describes how law, police and courts could work as market services in a stateless society, covering private law, polycentric law and objections.
jTYkdEU_B4o.why: HN commenters use it as a short introduction to anarcho-capitalist ideas about private law and how disputes could be resolved without a state.

j2Mu8qfVb5I.summary: A short clip of Dr. Robert Zubrin, author of The Case for Mars, answering why humanity should go to Mars. He argues that societies grow by challenging themselves and that exploration inspires young people.
j2Mu8qfVb5I.why: HN commenters repeatedly link it as the best concise answer to the question of why go to Mars when problems remain on Earth.

jEbRVNxL44c.summary: Real Engineering explains how Zipline built a drone delivery network for medical supplies in Rwanda. It covers the fixed-wing drones, catapult launch, parachute drop and the logistics behind the service.
jEbRVNxL44c.why: HN points to it as the best explanation of how Zipline's whole system works and as an example of drones doing real, useful work.

jN7mSXMruEo.summary: Not Just Bikes explains how SUVs and light trucks have grown in size and share of US sales, and why that is dangerous for pedestrians, cyclists and city life. He covers the regulatory loopholes, such as fuel economy rules and the chicken tax, that favored them.
jN7mSXMruEo.why: It is HN's default link whenever vehicle size comes up, with commenters recommending it for the history of the light-truck loophole and the safety effects of tall bumpers.

jcKRGpMiVTw.summary: Mathologer examines how identities like 1+2+3+... = -1/12 arise in Ramanujan's work, starting from his 1913 letter to Hardy. The video explains the rules for summing infinite series and why such results are meaningful but not naive sums.
jcKRGpMiVTw.why: Recommended as a careful, honest treatment of the -1/12 claim, often preferred over flashier videos.

jo_B4LTHi3I.summary: Ryan Dahl, the creator of Node.js, introduces the event-driven I/O framework built on V8 with examples, and discusses the v0.4.0 release and its new APIs.
jo_B4LTHi3I.why: Recommended as a short, fun talk on Node's philosophy and the reasons it was built that remains relevant.

jAhiMCSvtCc.summary: The first part of a long series documenting Dave Bull's Tokyo woodblock workshop as it produces a reproduction of Hokusai's The Great Wave. It follows the carving, proofing and printing of the reward print for Kickstarter backers.
jAhiMCSvtCc.why: HN commenters hold it up as a top-tier long-form process video, recommended whenever the Great Wave or Hokusai comes up.

jHP942Livy0.summary: Technology Connections explains how dishwashers work and how to use them well, including detergent use, the prewash cycle and why pre-rinsing hurts. It follows his earlier dishwasher videos.
jHP942Livy0.why: HN people recommend it as the definitive, thorough guide to getting dishwashers to clean properly and often send it to friends.

jwG_qR6XmDQ.summary: A three-minute clip of Jeff Bezos describing his Regret Minimization Framework: imagining yourself at 80 to decide whether to leave a Wall Street job to start Amazon.
jwG_qR6XmDQ.why: HN commenters cite it whenever someone asks whether to quit a job or start a company, as a simple decision heuristic.

j-vJxez9UF8.summary: AvE tears down a roughly $500 Dyson hair dryer, examining how its motor, airflow and electronics fit into a small body. He runs tests along the way and ultimately decides whether the engineering justifies the price.
j-vJxez9UF8.why: HN points to it as a favorite teardown, usually when discussing Dyson or how products are engineered and built, with some noting the host was impressed by the engineering.

j1I63wGcvU4.summary: First of a three-part tutorial series on the i3 tiling window manager for Linux. It explains what i3 is, how to install it on Ubuntu, and how to use it.
j1I63wGcvU4.why: HN commenters call it the best i3 tutorial on YouTube and recommend it for getting started thoroughly.

jVoSQP2yUYA.summary: Techmoan's beginner introduction to the compact cassette, testing metal tapes and Dolby S noise reduction on a Sony TC-S1 deck. He checks whether a cassette can sound close to a CD when good tape and equipment are used.
jVoSQP2yUYA.why: HN commenters cite it whenever cassette quality comes up, as proof that cassettes sound good with decent gear, metal tape and Dolby noise reduction.

jgOTZe07eHA.summary: David Kipping presents his proposed Terrascope, a telescope that uses Earth's atmosphere as a lens to achieve enormous magnification. He covers the history of telescopes and his path to the idea, plus Sol-scope and Jupiter-scope variants.
jgOTZe07eHA.why: HN people point to it as an excellent explanation of using Earth's atmosphere or gravity as a lens in astronomy threads.

jh8supIUj6c.summary: Aral Balkan's re:publica 2015 talk argues that people are the product of surveillance-based business models. It makes an ethical case against data monopolies and for privacy as a human right.
jh8supIUj6c.why: Recommended as a forceful statement of the privacy case, though some commenters found its tone elitist and politically charged.

j5v8D-alAKE.summary: Veritasium explores planned obsolescence, from the Phoebus lightbulb cartel to printers and phones. It explains how companies deliberately shortened product lifetimes and why products aren't better.
j5v8D-alAKE.why: Commenters link it as the engaging go-to explainer on planned obsolescence and the lightbulb cartel.

jA1C9VFqJKo.summary: Gary Garrett's stop-motion animation of his song Flying Dream, with notes arranged on a lattice of fifths and major thirds. It shows how harmony looks in just intonation, inspired by Harmonic Experience.
jA1C9VFqJKo.why: Shared as a beautiful example of lattice-based harmony visualization.

j4kI2h3iotA.summary: A long documentary-style video arguing that slavery in the US effectively continued through convict leasing and the prison system until around 1942. It covers the constitutional carveout and the history of neoslavery.
j4kI2h3iotA.why: Recommended in threads on prison labor and American history as a thorough account of the post-Civil War period.

jILgxeNBK_8.summary: A short animated TED-Ed lesson in which two competing ice cream vendors on a beach illustrate why rival shops cluster together. It introduces game theory and the Nash equilibrium through the Hotelling model.
jILgxeNBK_8.why: HN people use it as a clear, quick explanation of Nash equilibrium and why competitors cluster.

jMmUoZh3Hq4.summary: Technology Connections explains that US household power is split-phase, with two 120V legs that combine to 240V for large appliances. It covers the breaker panel and how the system works.
jMmUoZh3Hq4.why: HN commenters point to it to correct misconceptions about US voltage and to explain 240V availability in American homes.

jmTwlEh8L7g.summary: Christopher Domas presents research at DEF CON 26 showing a hidden alternate instruction set and undocumented hardware backdoor in some x86 processors, found on a third-party CPU. He uses it to ask how feasible wider hardware backdoors are.
jmTwlEh8L7g.why: HN regulars treat Domas as a favorite hacker and bring this talk up in any discussion of CPU backdoors, hidden instruction sets or processor security.

jqjacHSTd48.summary: Locksport historian Schuyler Towne's RVASec 2012 talk on why people lock their doors, tracing the history of locks and the assumptions about security behind them.
jqjacHSTd48.why: HN commenters call it a passionate and educational history of locks and physical security, and a good starting point for the subject.

j-kj2qwJa_E.summary: Bruce Hauman presents Figwheel, a ClojureScript tool for live, interactive development with hot code reloading. He explains the main ideas, demonstrates how it works, and shares tricks for getting the most out of it.
j-kj2qwJa_E.why: HN people point to it as a very visual demonstration of what hot-reloading and interactive development can offer, and as an example of a great dev tool pitch.

j6VlT_jUVPc.summary: James Hoffmann demonstrates his AeroPress technique with a short recipe: 11g of coffee, 200g of just-boiled water, a 2-minute immersion, then a press. He explains why he skips rinsing, preheating and inverting.
j6VlT_jUVPc.why: HN coffee fans cite it as a forgiving, repeatable recipe that gives good results.

j7zzQpvoYcQ.summary: Randy Pausch, a Carnegie Mellon computer scientist and virtual reality pioneer who was dying of cancer, gives his 'Last Lecture' about achieving childhood dreams and living well. The recording is a full-length talk of about 104 minutes.
j7zzQpvoYcQ.why: HN commenters recommend it as an emotionally powerful life-advice talk and revisit it as a reminder of mortality.

jOyfZex7B3E.summary: A look inside Dr Abrasive's lab as he engineers a flash-card replacement for the Sega Saturn optical drive after cracking its CD protection 20 years on.
jOyfZex7B3E.why: Recommended as an inspiring story of hardware reverse engineering and persistence.

jQIHqkudgNY.summary: A 70-minute video essay by Jimmy McGee on gambling, addiction and game design, tracing horse racing, slot machines and collectible card markets. It is the first in a series on making money from games.
jQIHqkudgNY.why: Recommended as an engaging, well-researched look at the history of gambling machines and how games borrow their psychology.

jlX_pThh7z8.summary: Tom Wildenhain's SIGBOVIK 2018 presentation of WordTeX, a Microsoft Word template that mimics LaTeX typesetting output. It is a joke research project executed with serious effort.
jlX_pThh7z8.why: HN people recommend it as an entertaining example of great effort on a trivial problem, and cite the template in LaTeX-versus-Word discussions.

jw8K460vx1c.summary: Revolution OS is a feature-length documentary on the history of free software and Linux. It covers Stallman and the GNU project, Torvalds and the kernel, and Raymond and Perens on open source, starting from the era of freely shared hobbyist code.
jw8K460vx1c.why: Recommended as the standard documentary on the origins of GNU, the FSF and Linux.

jzERXJgi5vQ.summary: A This Week in Startups episode in which Jason Calacanis interviews David Heinemeier Hansson of 37signals. They discuss bootstrapping, company philosophy and views on the tech industry.
jzERXJgi5vQ.why: Recommended to understand what the 37signals founders stand for and DHH's contrarian takes on tech business.

j02b8Fuz73A.summary: Steve Jobs demos NeXTSTEP Release 3, showing the object-oriented development environment and UI that later became the basis of Mac OS X. Midway through he builds a database-backed GUI app with Interface Builder and Enterprise Objects Framework with almost no code.
j02b8Fuz73A.why: HN uses it as the classic example of rapid visual app building and of a polished early Jobs presentation, often with timestamps pointing to the database demo.

j2dHFC31VtQ.summary: Not Just Bikes argues that oversized American fire trucks and fire department requirements push cities toward wide roads and dangerous street design. He compares this with the Dutch approach to emergency response.
j2dHFC31VtQ.why: HN people link it in threads on big vehicles and road safety as a comparison of US and Dutch fire department approaches.

j4H9LL7A-nQ.summary: Ben Felix argues that common beliefs about renting versus buying are wrong: homes are not great investments, mortgages are not a wealth hack, and ownership does not reliably bring happiness.
j4H9LL7A-nQ.why: Recommended as detailed math on rent versus buy, showing the choice is often roughly a wash.

jGWFg7EDnyY.summary: The Thought Emporium shows how to receive clear images directly from GOES-15, 16 and 17 and Himawari 8 geostationary weather satellites with software-defined radio. It covers the extra effort needed to receive GOES data.
jGWFg7EDnyY.why: HN commenters credit it for inspiring their own satellite-reception hobby and praise the channel's high-quality content.

jPhJbKBuNnA.summary: Tom Scott describes trying ChatGPT to fix his Gmail labels and being unsettled by how capable it was. He argues that we cannot know where we are on the technology curve, comparing it to Napster.
jPhJbKBuNnA.why: HN cites it for the argument that we cannot tell whether AI is early or late on its sigmoid curve until hindsight.

jSFsrmLhC00.summary: A complete remastered soundtrack for the Transport Tycoon 2014 mobile game, re-recorded with real instruments rather than the original MIDI. The music was composed by John Broomhall for the classic Transport Tycoon.
jSFsrmLhC00.why: Fans of Transport Tycoon and OpenTTD point to it as a nostalgic, live-instrument version of the game's music.

jSo5v5t4OQM.summary: A clip of psychologist Jordan Peterson lecturing on intelligence and IQ, covering how it is defined and its correlation with academic and work success.
jSo5v5t4OQM.why: HN commenters use it as supporting material in arguments about IQ and the g-factor view of intelligence.

jyQwgBAaBag.summary: Veritasium investigates whether a wind-powered vehicle can travel directly downwind faster than the wind, driving the Blackbird craft himself. The video explains the physics behind a claim some physics professors dispute.
jyQwgBAaBag.why: Frequently linked whenever wind-powered vehicles come up, as the clearest visual explanation of how the craft works.

j6ow-UemzBc.summary: Michael Bryzek of Flow gives a QCon London 2018 talk on key decisions for building maintainable microservices. It covers infrastructure, continuous deployment, communication, event streaming and language choice.
j6ow-UemzBc.why: HN commenters recommend it for showing the tooling possible when schemas and APIs are treated as code.

jAhjPd4uNFY.summary: Kurzgesagt's animated explainer on CRISPR gene editing, covering how the technology works and what it could mean for curing disease, designer babies and aging. It frames genetic engineering as an irreversible change coming to humanity.
jAhjPd4uNFY.why: HN commenters hand it out as a quick, accessible primer whenever CRISPR or gene editing comes up.

jhicDUgXyNg.summary: A live KEXP warm-up set by the Delvon Lamarr Organ Trio, recorded at Upstream Music Fest in 2017. The set includes Move On Up and Memphis.
jhicDUgXyNg.why: HN people recommend it as a great live KEXP session with standout guitar work and good sound.

jhnKBKZvb_U.summary: Leonard Susskind's Santa Fe Institute talk on the arrow of time: why the past differs from the future when physics equations are time-symmetric. He covers entropy, cosmology and Boltzmann brains.
jhnKBKZvb_U.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear explanation of why time runs one way, from a leading physicist.

j56s46e97Lo.summary: Trevor Paglen's 30C3 talk on photographing and documenting the secret state, including CIA flights, spy satellites and military sites, to reveal the geography of covert programs.
j56s46e97Lo.why: Recommended as a fascinating and still relevant look at the physical footprint of government secrecy.

j9uRckJLqLk.summary: Adam Savage shows off his collection of analog calculators, ending with a 3D-printed, scaled reproduction of the Curta mechanical calculator built by Marcus Wu. The video examines the replica and the engineering behind it.
j9uRckJLqLk.why: Linked whenever the Curta or mechanical calculators come up, as a look at a working 3D-printed version.

jAZapFzpP64.summary: Hank Green, a TikTok creator with millions of followers, explains why he thinks TikTok underpays creators. He compares its fixed-pot creator fund with YouTube's revenue sharing.
jAZapFzpP64.why: Cited in threads on creator economics as a clear explanation of how TikTok payouts shrink per creator as the platform grows.

jCC8fPQOaxU.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on mobile homes, showing how large investment companies are making this affordable housing option less affordable. It covers residents who rent land and cannot move their homes.
jCC8fPQOaxU.why: HN commenters point to it as good, accessible coverage of mobile-home park exploitation by private equity.

jK0BkTPUGQY.summary: Neurologist Dr. Matthew Phillips talks at Low Carb Gold Coast 2022 about fasting and ketogenic diets as therapies for cancer and neurodegenerative disease. He focuses on mitochondrial dysfunction and brain energy metabolism.
jK0BkTPUGQY.why: HN commenters point to it in threads on fasting, cancer and Alzheimer's as a clinician's overview of metabolic therapy.

jQOfbObFOCw.summary: A School of Life animated overview of Albert Camus, covering his existentialism and absurdism and his answer to the question of meaninglessness.
jQOfbObFOCw.why: Offered as an accessible introduction to Camus and absurdism.

jfOUVYQnuhw.summary: CGP Grey explains why airport codes are inconsistent and sometimes confusing, from their origins in old weather station codes to the quirks that cause mistakes. He builds the story around a single typo that sent a flight to the wrong continent.
jfOUVYQnuhw.why: HN people point to it as a fun summary of how messy airport codes are, especially in threads on aviation falsehoods and code collisions.

jf_ddGnum_4.summary: Jon Gjengset's roughly four-hour live stream implementing part of a BitTorrent client in Rust, following CodeCrafters' test-guided challenge. He builds from scratch and shows idiomatic error handling along the way.
jf_ddGnum_4.why: HN recommends it as a comprehensive walkthrough of the build-your-own-BitTorrent challenge and as an introduction to CodeCrafters.

jj8rMwdQf6k.summary: Peter Schiff's November 2006 speech to the Western Regional Mortgage Bankers Conference, in which he warned an audience of mortgage bankers that the housing bubble would collapse. The clip runs about 73 minutes.
jj8rMwdQf6k.why: HN cites it as a famous example of someone publicly predicting the housing crash before it happened.

jzMFoNZeZm0.summary: A long video essay arguing against the claim that Blazing Saddles could not be made today. It looks at the film as satire of the sanitized Western genre and what it did to that genre.
jzMFoNZeZm0.why: Pointed to as an informative rebuttal to the popular claim and as an explanation of the film's satirical effect on Westerns.

j2cMHwo3nAU.summary: A short demo of a playable Space Invaders game built inside Dwarf Fortress, with a downloadable map. It shows the game's mechanics used as a computing substrate.
j2cMHwo3nAU.why: HN cites it as an impressive example of building computation inside Dwarf Fortress.

j800SVeiS5I.summary: A 13-minute hand-animated short film that takes a symbolic journey through the unconscious, built around Carl Jung's idea of confronting the Shadow. It mixes 2D animation with spiritual and apocalyptic imagery.
j800SVeiS5I.why: Cited as a visual illustration of the Jungian shadow, including in arguments about national or collective shadows and conformity.

j973645y5AA.summary: Footage of an Airbus A380 engine blade-off test, in which a fan blade is deliberately released at full thrust to show the engine contains the failure.
j973645y5AA.why: Linked in aviation threads to show that engines are designed to contain a failed fan blade.

jBBS4FeY7XM.summary: A five-minute demo of the Common Lisp debugger fixing a bug, recompiling a single function, and resuming execution from the failed stack frame. It shows how to avoid re-running long computations.
jBBS4FeY7XM.why: HN Lisp fans repeatedly link it as a short, concrete demonstration of Common Lisp's interactive debugging advantage.

jErqdRE5zpQ.summary: A short Italian-language clip about the Canon Cat, a text-oriented personal computer from Canon designed by Jef Raskin, who started the Macintosh project. It shows the machine in use.
jErqdRE5zpQ.why: HN uses it as a quick look at what using a Canon Cat was actually like, in threads on Raskin, command interfaces and early Macintosh history.

jNa3axo40qM.summary: A four-minute Emacs Rocks screencast demonstrating the multiple-cursors package for Emacs. It shows how editing at many places at once can replace repetitive manual edits.
jNa3axo40qM.why: Cited as the canonical demo of multiple cursors and of fluent, efficient Emacs editing.

jWWGmiZs4JA.summary: Thunderf00t goes through the three UFO videos released by the Pentagon and offers mundane explanations for each. He treats the footage as sensor artifacts, parallax and camera effects rather than alien craft.
jWWGmiZs4JA.why: HN commenters use it as the go-to debunking of the Navy UFO videos, though one commenter also praises it as entertaining.

jXf04bhcjbg.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on tech monopolies, their hidden harms and possible remedies such as antitrust reform. John Oliver covers lobbying and legislation along the way.
jXf04bhcjbg.why: Cited as a mainstream summary of antitrust arguments and tech-company behavior in related threads.

jaoQh6BoH3c.summary: Joseph Henrich's Talks at Google presentation of his book. He argues that human success comes from collective brains and cultural learning across generations rather than individual intelligence.
jaoQh6BoH3c.why: Cited to support the view that human progress comes from networks and social learning.

jbp3kdJZ1_A.summary: A 105-minute technical deep dive from Noise In Space evaluating whether Starlink satellites could work as synthetic aperture radar. It covers SAR signal-to-noise, amplifiers, antennas, duplexing, phased array beamforming and simulations of V2 Mini and V3 satellites.
jbp3kdJZ1_A.why: Cited as a rigorous radio-engineering analysis of what radar capability Starlink could plausibly have.

jcvd5JZkUXY.summary: A two-minute animated minute meme by Nina Paley, photographed at the Metropolitan Museum, showing how all creative work builds on what came before. It is set to music from the Sita Sings the Blues soundtrack.
jcvd5JZkUXY.why: Used in copyright and AI-code debates to argue that creativity is inherently derivative.

jeRgFqbBM5E.summary: A PBS Space Time episode asking whether our universe could sit inside a black hole. It covers what physicists think happens inside black holes and the arguments for and against this idea.
jeRgFqbBM5E.why: Pointed to as a clear treatment of the universe-in-a-black-hole idea whenever black hole cosmology comes up.

jeghGhVdt9s.summary: LockPickingLawyer shows what happens when liquid gallium is applied to an aluminum Abus padlock, which weakens and breaks the metal. It is a short demonstration of gallium's effect on aluminum.
jeghGhVdt9s.why: HN points to it whenever gallium or liquid metal comes up, as a vivid demonstration of gallium destroying aluminum.

jltnBOrCB7I.summary: A clip of Milton Friedman answering an audience member about Ford's decision not to recall the Pinto, in which he defends weighing safety costs against benefits. The uploader's framing is strongly hostile to Friedman.
jltnBOrCB7I.why: HN uses it as an example of cost-benefit reasoning about product safety in threads on recalls, security spending and Boeing.

joMK1WZjP7g.summary: An IIHS crash test pitting a 1959 Chevrolet Bel Air against a 2009 Malibu in a frontal offset collision for the institute's 50th anniversary. The old car's occupant space collapses while the modern car's protects its driver.
joMK1WZjP7g.why: Commenters cite it as stark evidence that modern cars are far safer than older ones, countering nostalgia for 'built like they used to'.

jofycaXByTc.summary: A short animated explanation of the power split device in Toyota-style hybrids, a planetary gearset that works as an eCVT. It shows how engine and motor power are combined.
jofycaXByTc.why: HN people link it in hybrid versus EV debates as a clear view of how simple the hybrid drivetrain really is.

jpNU72dny2s.summary: Pediatric endocrinologist Robert Lustig talks at Low Carb Denver 2020 about sugar, metabolic syndrome and cancer. He lays out the case that metabolic dysfunction drives disease.
jpNU72dny2s.why: HN commenters recommend it as a Lustig lecture on sugar and metabolic disease, and as a source for claims about metabolic causes of weight gain.

jtMWEiCdsfc.summary: The first episode of the BBC's 1982 television series The Computer Programme, introducing home computing to a general audience. It surveys mainframes, early personal computers such as the BBC Micro and Commodore PET, and the changing computer market of the time.
jtMWEiCdsfc.why: Cited as nostalgic period documentation of the early UK microcomputer era, with commenters fondly remembering the series and the BBC Micro.

juWaO5TJS00.summary: A tour of Christian Schallert's 24 square meter apartment in Barcelona, designed so that it looks like an empty cube until he builds the furniture he needs. Kirsten Dirksen shows how the space is transformed for cooking, sleeping and dressing.
juWaO5TJS00.why: HN people link it as an example of a transformable small apartment in threads on micro-apartments and space-saving furniture.

jusWW2pPnA0.summary: A Graphics Programming Conference talk on how the game Tiny Glade renders meadows, trees and player-built castles. It covers real-time global illumination, tilt-shift depth of field, stable shadows with continuous time of day, ray marching and GPU-driven rendering on old hardware.
jusWW2pPnA0.why: Cited as a talk full of rendering tricks, and as an example of what a small team can do with custom tech.

jxNM4DGBRMU.summary: Practical Engineering summarizes the 2017 Oroville Dam spillway failure, explaining the engineering details behind the incident. It also discusses how operators and regulators failed to keep downstream residents safe.
jxNM4DGBRMU.why: Pointed to as a detailed engineering walkthrough of a major dam incident, and as a parallel to software failures.

jziQBWQxvok.summary: Kefrens' Desert Dream, an Amiga demoscene production released at The Gathering in 1993, recaptured in HD at 50fps. It features code, music and graphics by a team of scene members.
jziQBWQxvok.why: Brought up in Amiga threads as a classic example of what the demoscene achieved on old hardware.

j0UnS3jHhAA.summary: A short demo of a GPT-powered Linux shell that guesses the bash command you meant and sometimes hallucinates absurd results. The creator stresses that it is real and should not be trusted.
j0UnS3jHhAA.why: Cited as an early, amusing example of LLM-driven command-line toys, with commenters sharing similar experiments.

j0z4FweCy4M.summary: Tesla's 2021 AI Day presentation covering vision, planning and control, auto-labeling, simulation, the Dojo training hardware and the Tesla Bot announcement, followed by a Q&A.
j0z4FweCy4M.why: Treated as a primary source on how Tesla builds its self-driving stack, cited by timestamp for transformers, synthetic data, Dojo and the humanoid bot.

j4XT-l-_3y0.summary: A short clip of Bill Clinton's grand jury testimony in which he says it depends on what the meaning of the word 'is' is. It comes from questioning about Monica Lewinsky.
j4XT-l-_3y0.why: HN mostly quotes the line as shorthand for hair-splitting over definitions, rather than recommending the video itself.

j9tlJAqMV7U.summary: Gor Nishanov's CppCon 2018 talk on using tiny C++ coroutines to hide memory latency, interleaving useful work while prefetches bring cache lines in from main memory.
j9tlJAqMV7U.why: Cited as a deep dive on coroutines for cache misses and on running huge numbers of coroutines without heap allocation.

jAdG-iTilWU.summary: An SNL Weekend Update sketch from 1988 in which Kevin Nealon reports from the All-Drug Olympics and weightlifter Phil Hartman pulls his arms off.
jAdG-iTilWU.why: Brought up as a joke in threads about doping and athletic performance.

jAfUI_hETy0.summary: A Cracked video about the experience of intervening in a violent stabbing attack and the lack of police protection afterwards.
jAfUI_hETy0.why: HN uses it as a pointer for the claim that US police have no legal duty to protect individuals.

jJT_CACIZqs.summary: A man with no flight instruction and only desktop flight simulator experience attempts to take off and land a Cessna 172, with a commercial airline instructor aboard who gives no help. The flight came out of a prop bet.
jJT_CACIZqs.why: HN cites it as real evidence for whether a non-pilot can land a plane, whenever the topic comes up.

jKS3MGriZcs.summary: A short parody that removes the laugh track from The Big Bang Theory to show how unfunny the scenes are without it.
jKS3MGriZcs.why: Mentioned critically, as evidence that the show's jokes are weak and lean on canned laughter.

jNQXAC9IVRw.summary: The first video ever uploaded to YouTube, in April 2005. Co-founder Jawed Karim stands in front of the elephants at the San Diego Zoo for about 19 seconds.

jVeagFmmwA0.summary: Toyota's short promo clip showing a Mirai carbon-fiber hydrogen tank shot with a .50 caliber round at point blank range. The bullet pierces the tank, which does not burst, and the gas simply escapes and disperses.
jVeagFmmwA0.why: Cited in hydrogen debates as evidence that pressurized hydrogen tanks do not necessarily explode when punctured.

jVhlJNJopOQ.summary: An SNL sketch in which Ryan Gosling's character is obsessed with the font choice (Papyrus) in the movie Avatar's title. It is a comedy bit about a widely mocked typeface.
jVhlJNJopOQ.why: Posted as a joke in threads about typefaces and typography.

jWTGsUyv8IE.summary: A short amateur clip of a Moscow grocery store from 1989, filmed by a visiting production worker. The shelves look sparse, and the uploader adds a note on the hard-working people living under a system that did not reward them.
jWTGsUyv8IE.why: Cited as visual evidence of Soviet command-economy scarcity, usually in arguments about choice and central planning.

jahtu1_idVU.summary: Louis Rossmann, an independent repair shop owner, explains a recurring MacBook logic board design problem that leads to failures such as a black screen. The video is part of his right-to-repair advocacy.
jahtu1_idVU.why: Mostly used as an example in repair debates, with commenters calling the design an oversight or an anti-repair tactic.

jdM3ID4m38U.summary: Lindybeige's long video on Napoleon's most effective opponent, Sir Sidney Smith, with plenty of detail on Napoleon's misdeeds along the way.
jdM3ID4m38U.why: Cited by commenters as a source of examples of Napoleon's cruelty and poor decisions.

jf9I04Oa-hU.summary: A Nathan For You sketch in which Nathan Fielder tackles customers' privacy fears at computer repair shops with an awkwardly absurd business solution. It is a comedy clip from the Comedy Central show.
jf9I04Oa-hU.why: HN uses it only as a joke when computer repair privacy comes up.

jfPzUgzrOcQ.summary: Chess master Yosha Iglesias presents an analysis of Hans Niemann's games, highlighting a string of 100% engine-correlation games and comparing them with other players. It was published during the 2022 Niemann-Carlsen cheating scandal.

jgYYOUC10aM.summary: A one-minute Key & Peele sketch about planning a heist with a foolproof plan that has one small flaw.
jgYYOUC10aM.why: HN commenters use it only as a joke reference when a thread's scheme or fraud sounds like the sketch.

jhninL_G3Fg.summary: A scene from My Fair Lady in which Professor Higgins meets Colonel Pickering and Doolittle, singing about how the English fail to speak their own language properly. It has English subtitles.
jhninL_G3Fg.why: Cited as the classic illustration of accent, class and prejudice in how people speak.

ji3Hii_LZOc.summary: A one-minute clip showing an injury from a DJI Phantom 2 drone with stiff carbon fiber propellers. It is a warning about hobby drone safety.
ji3Hii_LZOc.why: Cited in drone regulation discussions as evidence that quadcopters can injure people.

jkhBlmKtEAk.summary: A two-minute NVIDIA RTX tech demo built on Remedy's Northlight engine, showing real-time ray-traced lighting and shadows in a game scene. It was shown alongside the launch of RTX and DirectX Raytracing.

jlPEBROvR9w.summary: A dramatization of a hypothetical Soviet first strike that destroys US bombers and Minuteman missiles, filmed with US Air Force cooperation. It is a short version of the 1979 documentary First Strike.

jnZ2NNYySuE.summary: A live performance at AGDQ 2014 in which Super Mario World is made to execute arbitrary injected code, running other games like Pong and Snake on the cartridge. It is done through a TASBot feeding precise controller inputs.

jrFv1O4dbqY.summary: A short claymation music video by animator savannahXYZ satirizing how bad web search has become, with SEO spam and ads crowding out real answers. It is comedic rather than analytical.

jrnRU3ocIH4.summary: An AP clip from October 2008 of John McCain correcting a town hall questioner who called Barack Obama an Arab, telling her Obama is a decent family man. It is a brief campaign trail moment.
jrnRU3ocIH4.why: HN cites it as an example of dignified political discourse and of a Republican defending an opponent.

jsLUidiYm0w.summary: The Office Space scene where Peter is grilled by his bosses for missing the cover sheet on his TPS report.
jsLUidiYm0w.why: Used as shorthand for pointless corporate nagging and soulless office life.

jvqFAi7vkBc.summary: Lex Fridman interviews OpenAI CEO Sam Altman about GPT-4, GPT-5, Sora, the OpenAI board saga, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever, power and AGI. The conversation runs nearly two hours.
